title: Aggregator development
description:
I’m looking to build a centralized review aggregation and analytics platform for my restaurant group. The goal is to automatically collect customer reviews from major review platforms, analyze the feedback using AI, and provide a dashboard that breaks down performance in areas such as food quality, service, operations, and guest satisfaction across multiple locations.

Below is a detailed outline of what I’m looking for.

---

## 1. Objective
Build an internal system that:

1. Automatically pulls customer reviews from major platforms.
2. Stores all reviews in a centralized database.
3. Uses AI/NLP analysis to identify sentiment and operational issues.
4. Provides a dashboard with insights and trends.
5. Sends alerts when serious complaints appear.
6. Works across multiple restaurant locations.

This system should function as a “Voice of the Customer” intelligence tool for management.

---

## 2. Platforms to Integrate

The system should automatically pull reviews from the following sources where API access is available.

Primary platforms:
- Google Reviews (Google Business Profile API)
- Yelp
- TripAdvisor
- Facebook Reviews

Secondary platforms (if possible):
- DoorDash merchant reviews
- Uber Eats merchant reviews
- Grubhub
- OpenTable
- Toast / POS integrated feedback
- Internal survey forms or website feedback

If some platforms have strict API limitations (such as Yelp), we should still capture what is legally accessible through their APIs and store it internally for analysis.

---

## 3. Review Collection Requirements

The system should:

• Automatically pull new reviews daily (or hourly)
• Support multiple restaurant locations
• Store full review text and metadata

Data fields to store for each review:

- Review ID
- Platform source
- Restaurant location
- Author name
- Rating (stars)
- Review text
- Review date
- Platform URL
- Owner response (if present)
- Raw JSON from API

All reviews should be normalized into a single schema regardless of the platform source.

---

## 4. Database Structure

Recommended tables:

### Locations
- location_id
- restaurant_name
- brand
- city/state
- platform IDs (Google location ID, Yelp business ID, etc.)

### Reviews
- review_id
- platform_source
- platform_review_id
- location_id
- rating
- author
- review_text
- review_date
- review_url
- raw_api_payload

### Review Analysis
- review_id
- sentiment_score
- food_score
- service_score
- operations_score
- value_score
- urgency_flag
- tags_json
- summary

---

## 5. AI Analysis Layer

Each review should be automatically analyzed using AI/NLP.

The system should classify reviews into the following categories:

### Sentiment
- Positive
- Neutral
- Negative

### Food Quality
Examples:
- taste
- freshness
- temperature
- portions
- consistency

### Service
Examples:
- friendliness
- attentiveness
- professionalism
- speed

### Operations
Examples:
- cleanliness
- wait time
- order accuracy
- drive-thru performance

### Value
Examples:
- price complaints
- portion size complaints

---

## 6. Issue Tagging

The system should automatically tag common restaurant issues such as:

Food Issues
- cold food
- undercooked
- bad taste
- stale ingredients

Service Issues
- rude staff
- slow service
- inattentive server

Operations Issues
- long wait time
- incorrect order
- dirty dining room
- drive-thru delays

---

## 7. Dashboard Requirements

Create a dashboard that allows management to quickly understand performance across locations.

### Overview Dashboard

Show:

• Average rating by location
• Rating trends over time
• Total reviews by platform
• Overall sentiment breakdown

---

### Complaint Analysis

Display:

Top complaints by frequency.

Example:

Slow service – 32 mentions
Cold food – 19 mentions
Wrong order – 17 mentions

---

### Location Comparison

Table example:

Location | Food Score | Service Score | Operations Score | Overall Rating

---

### Trend Tracking

Track changes over time:

- Weekly sentiment trends
- Monthly complaint trends
- Platform rating trends

---

## 8. Staff Mention Detection

If reviews mention specific employees or managers, the system should detect and track those names.

Example output:

Server John – 8 mentions (7 positive)
Manager Sarah – 3 mentions (1 negative)

---

## 9. Alerts for Critical Reviews

The system should automatically flag serious reviews and notify management when certain keywords appear.

Examples:

Food safety:
- raw food
- food poisoning
- sick

Serious service complaints:
- discrimination
- harassment
- racist

Refund risk:
- never coming back
- worst experience

Alerts can be sent via:
- Email
- Slack
- SMS (optional)

---

## 10. Owner Response Assistance

The system should generate suggested responses to reviews that management can approve before posting.

Example:

Review:
“Food was great but service was slow.”

Suggested response:
“Thank you for your feedback. We're glad you enjoyed the food and apologize for the delay in service. We're working with our team to improve wait times and hope to see you again soon.”

---

## 11. Weekly Executive Reports

Automatically generate weekly summaries.

Example insights:

Top complaints this week
Best performing location
Location needing attention
Review volume trends

Reports should be emailed automatically to management.

---

## 12. Technical Architecture (Suggested)

Backend:
- Python (FastAPI) or Node.js

Database:
- PostgreSQL

Hosting:
- AWS / Google Cloud / Supabase

AI Analysis:
- OpenAI API or similar NLP service

Dashboard:
- Metabase
- Power BI
- or custom React dashboard

Automation:
- Scheduled jobs to pull reviews daily

---

## 13. Future Expansion

The system should be designed so we can add features later such as:

- Voice of Customer score
- Predictive review trend analysis
- Integration with POS sales data
- Integration with employee scheduling
- Multi-brand support

---

## 14. End Goal

The goal is to create a centralized review intelligence platform that allows us to understand:

• What customers like most
• What operational problems occur most often
• Which locations are performing best or worst
• Where service improvements are needed

This system should ultimately help improve customer satisfaction, operational performance, and reputation management.

---

Please let me know your thoughts on architecture, timeline, and estimated cost for development.
